findings.description: The database username and password are interpolated into EC2 user data and written into a local configuration file. User data is retrievable through instance metadata and AWS control-plane APIs by principals with appropriate describe access, exposing the database credential beyond a secrets-management boundary.

No metadata_options block requires IMDSv2, so the instance can use IMDSv1. A server-side request forgery flaw in the web application could retrieve instance metadata credentials without IMDSv2 session-token protection.

publicly_accessible is set to true, assigning the RDS instance a public endpoint. Although the shown security group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to internet-reachable network paths and makes later security-group changes capable of exposing it publicly.
storage_encrypted is explicitly false, leaving database storage, automated backups, snapshots, and replicas unencrypted at rest.

This rule allows all protocols and ports from the database security group to 0.0.0.0/0. It creates an unrestricted outbound channel from the database network interface that can be used for data exfiltration or command-and-control if the database environment is compromised.

The EC2 application role grants every S3, EC2, and RDS action on every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would permit broad account-level resource access and potentially destructive actions.
